source_refs.note: Topic 25.6.1 (PDF 241-242); Figure 25.11 is replaced by an original labelled schematic. The key trees listed (yew, blue pine, cedar) are evergreen conifers rather than leaf-shedding trees; the lesson keeps the book's list.

blocks.text: These forests grow in moist mountain regions with distinct seasons, including a cold winter in which the trees drop their leaves (deciduous).

blocks.alt: A simple labelled landscape of a temperate deciduous forest beside an information card.
blocks.caption: The temperate deciduous forest: a labelled schematic and fact card (original diagram).
blocks.long_description: A forested mountain slope with broad-leaved and conifer trees and a stream. The card gives the location (Shogran, Neelam Valley, Murree, Kaghan), climate (4 to 30 C, 750-1500 mm of rain) and grey-brown humus-rich soil, plants (yew, blue pine, Himalayan cedar, Berberis lyceum), animals (rhesus monkey, black bear, leopard cat, wolves, birds) and status (degraded by the timber industry and farming).

blocks.caption: Profile of the temperate deciduous forest
rows: northern areas: Shogran, Neelam Valley, Murree, parts of Kaghan
rich, grey-brown soil high in organic matter (humus)
moderate, 4 to 30 C; 750-1500 mm of rain a year
Taxus baccata (yew), Pinus wallichiana (blue pine), Cedrus deodara (Himalayan cedar); shrubs such as Berberis lyceum (sumbal)
rhesus monkey (Macaca mulatta), black bear, leopard cat, wolves, many birds
degraded: many large predators wiped out; pressure from the timber industry and farming

blocks.prompt: Name one plant and one animal of the temperate deciduous forest.
blocks.explanation: For example Taxus baccata (yew) and rhesus monkey (Macaca mulatta).
